description: Attack the launch-overhead-bound small-n shapes (n=32,176,352): replace torch.geqrf with a single fused Triton kernel doing unblocked Householder QR, one program per matrix, eliminating cuSOLVER's thousands of tiny launches + D2H copies. n<=176 fits whole-matrix in SMEM (176^2*4=124KB); n=352 (496KB) exceeds SMEM so panel-stream columns through SMEM/registers. Per column: norm, reflector v (LAPACK convention: alpha=-sign(a_kk)||x||, v[k]=1 implicit, tau in [0,2]; zero/tiny norm => tau=0,v=e_k for rank-deficient/collinear), rank-1 trailing update on-chip. Write H (R on/above diag, v below) + FP32 tau matching geqrf shapes. Householder is backward-stable so all conditioning cases pass; correctness hinges on the exact sign/zero-column convention. Route n>=512 and every off-grid n to torch.geqrf. Avoid the literal substring 'stream' anywhere in source.

Attack the dominant n=512/1024 large-batch shapes with blocked right-looking Householder QR using the compact-WY representation, batched ACROSS all matrices. A Triton kernel factors each b-column panel (b~32-64) for ALL matrices at once (one CTA per matrix's panel => 640 CTAs in flight = full occupancy, the lever cuSOLVER misses) and forms the b x b triangular T factor; apply the block reflector A := A - V T (V^T A) to the trailing submatrix as batched torch.bmm GEMMs (tensor cores). Keep GEMM in cuBLAS/bmm, NOT Triton (cuBLAS wins flops). The ONLY mandatory-Triton part is the batched panel factorization. Far fewer, larger launches than cuSOLVER's per-matrix path. Use LAPACK reflector/sign/zero-column convention; emit FP32 (H,tau) exactly like geqrf. Route off-grid n to torch.geqrf; avoid substring 'stream'.

Attack n=512 (the runtime-dominant shape, batch=640) occupancy-first, a mechanism distinct from blocked-BLAS3: a fully-fused batched geqr2 Triton kernel with ONE CTA per matrix, all 640 resident => full occupancy, ZERO inter-CTA sync and ZERO global trailing-update GEMM. The profile shows cuSOLVER ~100x off FP32 peak here = launch/batch-bound, not flops/HBM, so trade tensor-core GEMM throughput for zero launch overhead. n=512 FP32 = 1MB/matrix exceeds SMEM, so stream column panels through SMEM + registers, each CTA factoring its matrix end-to-end (unblocked or small-panel Householder). LAPACK convention: alpha=-sign(a_kk)||x||, v[k]=1 implicit, tau in [0,2], zero-norm column => tau=0,v=e_k. Emit FP32 (H,tau) like geqrf. Route off-grid n to torch.geqrf; avoid the substring 'stream' in source identifiers/comments.

Branch off the GLOBAL BEST (d381eef6, worker1's Triton blocked compact-WY, 11314us) and extend it to the n=1024 batch=60 shapes, now the dominant geomean term (~90827us x3). PROFILE n=1024 FIRST to split panel-kernel vs trailing-GEMM time. Expect the one-CTA-per-matrix panel factorization to starve the GPU at b=60 (~60 CTAs vs ~188 SMs), so the PRIMARY lever is multi-CTA-per-matrix (or 2-level/recursive blocking) on the panel kernel to cover the SMs; SECONDARY: widen panels to amortize the ~32 serial panel launches. Keep the trailing GEMM FP32 with TF32 OFF (Blackwell FP32 already uses tensor cores) - bf16 only as a gated experiment that MUST clear orthogonality on nearrank/mixed n=1024 with margin (rtol=100*n*eps32, no atol). Do NOT reduce CTA count (multiple matrices per CTA is the wrong direction here). Keep LAPACK (H,tau), route off-grid n to torch.geqrf, no 'stream' substring.

Branch off the GLOBAL BEST (fbaabbf9, two-level blocked Triton QR, 5870us) and extend its custom path to the UNTOUCHED n=2048(batch=8) and n=4096(batch=2) shapes, which every candidate still routes to torch.geqrf (~74700us & ~50400us - now the TWO LARGEST per-shape terms). KEY INSIGHT: the baseline profile shows cuSOLVER's FP32 trailing update uses NON-tensor-core kernels (cutlass d884/SIMT sgemm) - the exact lever that won n<=1024 (FP32 torch.bmm hits Blackwell tensor cores while cuSOLVER doesn't). At n=2048 each matrix's trailing GEMM is huge, so this lever can transfer even at low batch where the panel under-occupies. Stay Triton (panel kernel) + batched bmm/baddbmm trailing update, wide outer block, FP32 TF32-OFF (do NOT use bf16/fp16 - worker 2 already proved low-bit storage fails the factor gate on rankdef/clustered). PROFILE custom-vs-geqrf at these sizes FIRST; explicit kill-criterion: if the custom path cannot beat geqrf by >5% after a genuine attempt, that is a SETTLED result - keep routing n>=2048 to geqrf and return. Emit LAPACK (H,tau); route off-grid n to geqrf; no 'stream' substring.

Branch off the GLOBAL BEST (fbaabbf9, two-level Triton QR, 5870us) and replace the trailing-update GEMM PRIMITIVE - the single largest cost (~55% of n=512 b=640 time), confirmed compute-bound. cuBLAS torch.bmm picks a SIMT path (cutlass_simt/magma_sgemmEx, NOT tensor-core) for the skinny-K (nb=16/NB=64) FP32 batched trailing update; cuBLAS choosing SIMT does NOT mean SIMT is optimal. Write a custom Triton tl.dot FP32 GEMM specialized for this exact skinny-K batched shape (A -= V (T^T (V^T A))), tuned tiling/occupancy for K in {16,64}, ideally fusing the V^T A and V (..) products and the subtract to cut HBM round-trips vs the 3-bmm+baddbmm chain. This is orthogonal to workers 1 (blocking algorithm) and 2 (n>=2048) - nobody owns the GEMM primitive. PROFILE to confirm the GEMM is compute-bound (not launch-bound - at b=640 launches are amortized) BEFORE committing. Keep FP32 with input_precision='ieee'/TF32-off (bf16/TF32 fail the factor gate on nearrank/mixed); emit LAPACK (H,tau); route off-grid + n>=2048 to geqrf; no 'stream' substring. Secondary if the GEMM doesn't pay: CUDA-graph capture of the host panel loop to help the small-batch shapes.

Replace the trailing bmm chain with a custom Triton tl.dot GEMM at input_precision='tf32x3'.
